title: Observability workbench: cost + trace deep-dive (week of 2026-06-22)
content:
Purpose and context:
This note captures the workbench session and follow-ups from the observability deep-dive on cost drift correlated with tracing signal changes. We ran an initial set of queries and short experiments to validate an emerging hypothesis: a recent rollout of more aggressive KV-cache eviction + a trace sampling tweak coincided with a sustained small uptick in per-token tracing cost and dashboard query latency across a subset of hosted customers.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Symptom: ~6–9% increase in trace-related query cost (BigQuery/Clickhouse egress + ingestion compute) starting 2026-06-10, persistent.
- Observed at same time: 15–25% increase in average trace span size for long-tail requests, and rise in KV cache miss rate on the serving runtime for traces containing heavy tool-calls.
- Likely cause (working hypothesis): config change in span sampling + default KV cache TTL rollback rolled out in small canary on 2026-06-08. That increased sampled span retention and increased exported trace payloads; downstream processors ran longer aggregation windows causing heavier query load.
- Immediate mitigation: revert the KV cache TTL for tracing metadata to previous value in canary and throttle aggregator windows for affected ingestion cluster (deployed 2026-06-24). We will monitor 48–72h.

Data snapshots we pulled during session (high-level):
- Trace export bytes (hosted ingestion cluster A): baseline (May avg) 1.1 TB/day -> 1.18 TB/day (June 11–20) -> 1.25 TB/day (June 21–23)
- Avg span count per request (p99 cohort): May 6.8 -> June 12–20 7.5 -> 8.3 (long tail)
- KV cache miss rate (serving runtime for trace keys): went from 3.6% -> 7.9% post-change on canary nodes
- Aggregator CPU 95th: +22% in the affected ingestion pool

Why this matters:
- Cost: trace ingestion and downstream OLAP queries are a non-trivial fraction of the shared telemetry bill; sustained drift erodes our margin and complicates usage-based pricing forecasts.
- UX: Dashboard load times for model-debug dashboards increased (user report from SEs and a client-reported slower trace waterfall experience).
- Reliability: higher ingestion CPU correlates with increased backpressure and occasional sample drops (observed modestly during the spike windows).

Hypotheses and evidence matrix:
1) Hypothesis: Sampling policy change increased retained spans.
   Evidence: rollout log shows sampling policy bump in canary on 2026-06-08 (CON-1721). Trace volumes and avg span count rose post-rollout.

2) Hypothesis: KV-cache TTL rollback caused more upstream lookups and larger serialized traces to be exported.
   Evidence: runtime config diff (PR in repo) indicates TTL change for trace meta keys; runtime metrics show cache miss rate doubled on canary nodes.

3) Alternative: Client-side behavior (some customers started large batch debug requests).
   Evidence: customer-region breakouts do not align to a single tenant spike — increase is broad but proportionally larger in customers using tool-calls. Customer CS reports show no coordinated debugging campaigns.

Experiments / steps taken during the session (and immediate results):
- Reverted KV-cache TTL on canary pool to previous setting (rolled back 2026-06-24 18:30 PDT). Early telemetry (6h window) shows canary miss-rate dropped from 7.9% -> 3.9% and exported bytes dipped ~3.5%. Not a full return to baseline yet.
- Throttled aggregator batch window from 60s -> 120s for ingestion cluster B to smooth CPU peaks (deployed 2026-06-24 19:10 PDT). This reduced 95th CPU by ~8% in first 3h.
- Added a temporary low-sampling filter for requests coming from the 'tools-heavy' traffic tag to limit p99 span explosion while we assess quality impact.

Dashboard and instrumentation actions (what we changed and why):
- Added a dedicated "trace-cost workbench" dashboard tile that cross-correlates: exported bytes, avg span count (p50/p95/p99), KV cache miss rate, aggregator CPU 95th, and per-query latency for model-debug dashboards. This is pinned on Observability home and shared with SEs.
- Created a synthetic job (obs/synth/trace-load) that replays representative traced sessions at 10x to validate aggregator behavior under controlled conditions. First run scheduled 2026-06-26 03:00 UTC.
- Added an alert: trace-export-bytes-rate > 15% above 7-day rolling baseline for 3 intervals triggers a runbook paging to eng-observability on-call (severity P3).

Open questions and risks:
- Quality regressions: does dropping sampling/throttling tools-heavy traces degrade our ability to diagnose customer issues? Need to evaluate the delta on triage time for SEs. (Action: Marta will run a 2-week retrospective on triages for high-value customers to compare signal loss.)
- Billing attribution: is the increased cost fully trace-related (ingest + OLAP) or are there secondary effects (more dashboard query retries, longer user sessions)? (Action: Ben to run a cost-attribution query across telemetry and query logs.)
- Rollout policy: our config rollout and canary visibility gap allowed this to reach multi-pool exposure before we noticed. Should we add synthetic canary generators to detect span-size regressions proactively? (Action: Ethan to draft an RFC for synthetic canaries and detection hooks.)

Action items (owner, date):
- Monitor canary revert telemetry and produce 48h report (Aisha) — due 2026-06-26.
- Execute synthetic trace-load job and validate aggregator behavior (Samir + Marta) — scheduled 2026-06-26 run; summary due 2026-06-27.
- Cost attribution SQL + PR with annotated results (Ben) — due 2026-06-28.
- RFC for synthetic canaries and span-size alarms (Ethan) — draft by 2026-07-02.
- Update runbook with explicit trace sampling rollback steps and owner (Aisha) — due 2026-06-30.
- Communicate mitigations and potential UX impact to SE rotation and CS (Marta) — message drafted, send by 2026-06-25 EOD.

Notes for follow-up meeting (observability sync 2026-06-26):
- Bring 24h and 48h telemetry for canary revert plus synthetic job results.
- Decide on whether to widen rollback to all pools if 48h shows sustained improvement.
- Review SE impact log (Marta) and decide sampling guard thresholds.

Appendix (quick logs and queries used):
- Key queries: export_bytes_by_day.sql; span_count_percentiles.sql; kv_cache_miss_rate_by_node.sql; aggregator_cpu_95.sql. (See linked CON-1721 for raw query text.)
- Short links:
  - Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/478
  - Canaries list: CON-1721 (config rollout history)
  - Cost ticket: JIRA-OBS-812

Informal notes / ideas captured in the session (brainstorm):
- Could we add optional compressed trace summaries instead of full spans for tool-heavy calls? Trade-off: smaller export size vs potential debugging fidelity loss. Worth prototyping.
- Consider adding a "span-slim" serialization mode for long-tool calls where only key metadata is exported and full spans kept locally for 24h for on-demand fetch.

End of workbench note. Please add any corrections inline. We will sync 2026-06-26 at the weekly observability meeting to decide on rollout widening and final remediation path.
